info.name: Battle Service
info.description:
Every route of the Battle Service, in run order: a challenge is issued, accepted, fought turn by turn and resolved. The Setup folder registers its own users through User Management and befriends them, because a challenge is refused between users who are unrelated — so the collection needs no stored credential and can be run repeatedly.

Set userManagementUrl, battleUrl and serviceToken in the environment. The creature identifiers are collection variables: with DEPENDENCY_MODE=mock the mocked Tamagotchi Service derives a creature deterministically from its id, and these four resolve to level 20, which keeps the scripted match from ending before the last turn. Against a live Tamagotchi Service, replace them with creatures the two users own.

request.description: Battle refuses a challenge between users who are neither friends nor enemies, so the relationship has to exist first.

exec: // One assertion below depends on this: the mocked User Management reports every pair as
// friends, so the unrelated-users rule can only be exercised against the live service.
pm.test("the opponent's lineup is unknown until acceptance", () => pm.expect(battle.opponent.lineup == null).to.be.true);
pm.test("a pending battle has no current turn", () => pm.expect(battle.currentTurnUserId == null).to.be.true);

request.description: The relationship is read from User Management; this service does not decide it.

exec: // The mocked User Management reports every pair as friends, so the rule is only
// observable with DEPENDENCY_MODE=live. The assertion follows the configured mode
// instead of pretending the mock can produce the refusal.
pm.test("mocked: every pair is reported as friends, so the challenge is created", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
